what-is-an-ai-journal: Common questions
What is an AI journal?

An AI journal is a diary that can read back what you have written. You still write in your own words. The AI helps you find things, notice what has changed and talk entries through, starting from your own record rather than a blank chat.
What Everglow does with your entries
Ask your journal a question, such as “What did I decide about the move?”, and check the answer against the original entries.
Talk things through with a companion that draws on what you have written.
Revisit the people and places you write about, with the moments they appear in.
See a map of who connects to whom across your journal.
What it doesn’t do
It doesn’t write your entries for you.
It can make mistakes. Check important details against your original entries, and correct the AI when it misreads something.
Getting started
Start free with 7 journal entries and 10 companion chat turns. Bring older writing in through Markdown, plain-text, CSV or JSON import.
Is an AI journal the same as a chatbot?
No. A chatbot starts from nothing. An AI journal starts from your own record, so its answers are about your life.
Which AI does Everglow use?
You choose: an on-device model, your own API key, or optional Everglow Cloud.

offline-ai-journal: Common questions
Can an AI journal work offline?

Yes, with on-device AI. Everglow can run its AI model on your iPhone. After a one-time model download, you can write, ask your journal questions and talk with the companion without sending your words anywhere.
What needs a connection
The first model download, about 2.6 GB. It downloads over Wi-Fi only.
Your own API key or Everglow Cloud, if you choose either. Both are remote processing.
Optional iCloud backup.
What works without one
Writing, editing and searching your entries.
Asking your journal questions and chatting with the companion, using the on-device model.
Browsing the people, places and timeline Everglow builds from your writing.
The trade-offs

On-device AI depends on your iPhone. It is slower than hosted AI and needs storage for the model, and availability and performance vary by device. You can switch engines in Settings at any time, or write without AI.
Does Everglow need the internet?
Only for the model download, a remote engine you choose, or backup. With on-device AI, your journal and its AI features work without a connection.
Is on-device AI as good as hosted AI?
It keeps your writing on your iPhone and works offline. Hosted AI is usually faster and handles longer, more detailed questions better.

private-ai-journal: Common questions
Is an AI journal private?

It depends on where the AI runs. Everglow keeps your journal archive on your iPhone. With on-device AI, your writing stays there. With your own API key or Everglow Cloud, the context a request needs goes to that provider for processing.
Three engines, three answers
On-device AI
Your writing is processed on your iPhone. Nothing is sent anywhere for AI.
Your own API key
The context a request needs goes to the provider you choose, such as OpenAI, Claude, Gemini or DeepSeek. That provider’s policies and data terms apply.
Everglow Cloud
The request passes through Everglow’s hosted service to OpenAI. Everglow retains no content after the request completes.
Other privacy controls
App lock with Face ID or a passcode.
Optional iCloud backup, stored as an encrypted snapshot in your private CloudKit database.
Plain Markdown export, so your words are never locked in.
Does Everglow train AI on my journal?
No. Everglow never uses your writing to train any model. If you use your own API key, that provider’s data terms apply.
Can I use Everglow without AI?
Yes. You can keep a journal without asking any AI to process it.

rosebud-alternative: Switching from Rosebud
Looking for a Rosebud alternative?
Everglow is an iPhone AI journal with a small free start and a one-time unlock, no subscription required. Its AI runs on your iPhone, your own key or Cloud.
Verified against Everglow 1.5 on 10 October 2026.
What changed at Rosebud

Rosebud’s help center says its free plan was retired effective 30 September 2026. The reason it gives is a move to an upgraded experience with a new memory system that needs far more resources, which it says makes a free tier unsustainable. The same article says nothing users have written is going away, that entries can be exported at any time, and that free users can see a special offer in the Rosebud app.

On the US App Store, Rosebud lists in-app purchases for Rosebud Bloom at $12.99 and $107.99, Thrive 2x at $24.99 and $199.99, and Thrive 5x at $59.99 and $499.99. Its website presents Bloom as $12.99 a month or $107.99 a year, with a free trial. We read these pages on 10 October 2026; check them for current terms.
Rosebud help center: Changes to the Free Plan
Rosebud on the US App Store
Rosebud’s website, pricing section
What Everglow costs

Everglow is free to download, with no account to create. The free start is small: 7 journal entries and 10 companion chat turns, counted in total rather than per month. That is enough to try the app, not to keep a journal in it. After that there are two ways to continue, and you can choose either or both.
Everglow Unlimited
is a one-time purchase, $9.99 in the US, that permanently removes the entry and chat limits. It does not include hosted AI. You use it with on-device AI or your own API key.
Everglow Cloud

is an optional subscription for hosted AI with a monthly usage allowance: Standard at $2.99 a month or Pro at $5.99 a month in the US. It needs no model download or API key, and it lifts the entry and chat limits only while it is active.

Prices vary by storefront, and the app shows the current price before you buy. If you want to stop paying a monthly fee for journaling, the combination that does that is Unlimited with on-device AI. With your own API key, you pay that provider for what you use instead.
Where the AI runs
Everglow keeps your journal archive on your iPhone whichever engine you pick. You choose where the AI that reads it runs, you can switch in Settings, and you can write with no AI at all.
On your iPhone.

Google’s Gemma 4 E2B model runs through Google’s LiteRT-LM runtime. It is a one-time download of about 2.6 GB over Wi-Fi; after that, writing, Ask and the companion work offline. It is slower than hosted AI, and availability and performance depend on your device.
Your own API key.

Use a key from OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), Google (Gemini) or DeepSeek. The context a request needs goes to that provider, under its policies and charges. The app names the provider and asks for your consent before anything is sent, and keys are kept in the iOS Keychain.
Everglow Cloud.
Requests pass through Everglow’s hosted service to OpenAI. Everglow retains no content after a request completes.
Everglow never uses your writing to train any model, and its App Store privacy label reads “Data Not Collected”.

Bringing your Rosebud entries over

Rosebud’s Export data help page describes an Export option under Settings in its mobile app, and an Export button under “Export to Markdown” in Settings on the web. Everglow 1.5 imports Markdown, so that file is the place to start.
Export your entries from Rosebud, and keep that file as your own backup.
In Everglow, open Settings, then Import from another app, and choose the file or folder. It accepts Markdown, plain text, folders, ZIP, and CSV or JSON with field mapping. You can also paste text.
Review before anything is saved. You can edit an entry’s text and date, merge it into the previous entry, split it, or leave it out.
Confirm. Entries land on their original dates. One without a readable date goes to a queue for you to place later, never onto today, and importing the same file again won’t create duplicates.

Some limits to plan around. Everglow has no Rosebud-specific importer, and we haven’t tested a Rosebud export file, so check the dates in the review. Everglow reads a date from a heading line that is only a date, from a date or created field in front matter, or from a file name. Rosebud’s page doesn’t say what its export includes, so compare a few entries with the originals.

Imported entries count toward the free limit, so an import pauses when the free entries run out and waits in Settings until you unlock Unlimited or subscribe to Cloud. Each imported entry is also read by the AI engine you choose. On device, a few hundred entries can take a while, and the import continues in the background. With your own key, entry text goes to that provider. With Cloud, each entry uses part of the monthly allowance.
Rosebud help center: Export data
Is Everglow the same kind of app?

Not quite, and it helps to know before you move. Rosebud’s App Store listing describes it as “Daily Self-Care & Habits” in the Health & Fitness category. Everglow is a journal archive you can ask questions of.
Ask
answers questions across your journal at Fast or Considered depth and shows the dated excerpts it used.
People, places and things

get pages that collect what you have written about them, with each fact linked to the entry it came from. You can confirm, edit, pin or delete facts, and earlier values are kept rather than overwritten.
A companion
to talk with, in six editable personas, three reflective and three companion-style. It draws on your journal, and your conversations become part of the archive.

What Everglow does not do matters as much. It is not a guided therapy or coaching program, and it has no habit tracker or goal plans. It runs only on iPhone, with no Android app, web app or sync between devices. AI can make mistakes, so check important details against your original entries.
Rosebud’s billing help page
covers subscriptions on the web, iOS and Android. If you write in Rosebud on Android or the web, Everglow cannot follow you there.
Is Everglow free?

It is free to download, with 7 journal entries and 10 companion chat turns in total. To keep writing past that, buy Everglow Unlimited once ($9.99 in the US) or subscribe to Everglow Cloud, which lifts the limits only while it is active.
Can I import my Rosebud entries?

Yes, once you export them. Rosebud’s help center describes a Markdown export, and Everglow imports Markdown with a review step before anything is saved. There is no Rosebud-specific importer, so check the dates and a few entries in the review.
Does Everglow send my journal to an AI company?

Only if you choose a remote engine. With on-device AI, your writing is processed on your iPhone. With your own API key, the context a request needs goes to that provider. With Everglow Cloud, it passes through Everglow’s service to OpenAI, and Everglow keeps no content afterward.
Do I need a subscription to use AI in Everglow?
No. Everglow Unlimited with on-device AI has no ongoing payment. With your own API key, the provider bills you for usage. Everglow Cloud is the only subscription, and it is optional.
Does Everglow work on Android or the web?
No. Everglow is an iPhone app for iOS 17 or later. There is no Android or web version and no sync between devices. Optional iCloud backup is a snapshot for restoring, not live sync.

move-from-day-one: Moving from Day One
How do I move my Day One journal to Everglow?
Export your Day One journal as JSON, then import that file from Everglow’s Settings. Entries keep their dates and text, and tags become topics. Photos stay in Day One.
Verified against Everglow 1.5 on 10 October 2026.

Everglow 1.5 has no importer built for Day One. It reads Day One’s JSON and CSV files through its general importer, which recognizes their date and text fields on its own. The Day One steps below come from Day One’s help pages, read the same day.
Which Day One export to choose
Day One export
Everglow 1.5 reads it?
What carries over
JSON, from any Day One app
Yes, without setup
Date and time, full text, tags as topics
CSV, from iPhone or Android
Yes
Date and time, full text
Plain Text or Markdown
Not reliably
The whole export is one text file, so chosen as a ZIP it arrives as a single entry
PDF
No
Nothing

Choose JSON. Day One says its JSON files can contain all entries, media and metadata, and each entry in them carries a machine-readable date. CSV is the fallback: Day One’s CSV export holds only the date and the text. Day One lists what each format contains in its guide
Exporting entries
Step by step
Set up an AI engine in Everglow first.
The on-device model, your own API key or Everglow Cloud all work. Without one, imported entries are saved but not read, and the import pauses until an engine is ready.
Export from Day One.

On iPhone, open Settings → Import/Export, choose the journal, set a date range and choose JSON. On a Mac, Control-click the journal in the journal pane and choose Export, then JSON. The web and Windows apps export a whole journal from Edit Journal → Journal Settings → Export Journal.
Open the ZIP on your iPhone.
Save it to the Files app and tap it, and Files expands it into a folder, as Apple describes in
Create or open ZIP files
. Inside is a .json file, plus folders of photos and other media if you included them.
Import into Everglow.
Open Settings → Privacy & Data → Import from another app, tap Choose a file or folder, and pick the .json file.
Review before saving.

Each entry shows its date and first lines. Tap one to correct its text or date or to split it, and switch off any entry you don’t want. If you have more than one engine set up, choose the one that reads the entries under Runs on. Then tap the Import button.
Let it run.
The import continues in the background and picks up again if you quit Everglow. At the end, a summary counts the entries imported, any skipped as already imported, and any that failed.

Choosing the ZIP itself also works for a small export of a single journal. The .json file is the safer pick: Everglow 1.5 reads only one .json file from a ZIP, and a large ZIP full of media may not open at all.
Try a small sample first

Before you move years of writing, import a short stretch. Day One on iPhone and Android can export a date range; on a Mac, select a range of entries in List view and export just those. Then compare the sample in Everglow with Day One: the number of entries, a few dates and a few complete texts.

On the free tier, keep the sample to 7 entries or fewer, because imported entries count toward the 7 free entries. When the sample looks right, export the rest. Entries you already imported are skipped the second time, as long as their text and day haven’t changed.
What carries over
The full text of every entry.
The date and time Day One recorded. Entries land on those dates, not on the day you import them.
Tags, which become topics on each entry. This needs the JSON export, because Day One’s CSV has no tags.
After import, Everglow reads each entry the way it reads new writing, so your Day One years become part of Ask, search and the pages for people and places.
What changes on the way
Titles.
Day One’s export has no separate title field. A title is the first line of the text, usually marked with #, and it stays the first line in Everglow, # included.
Formatting marks.
Day One writes entry text as Markdown and puts a backslash before some punctuation, so a sentence can end in \. instead of a plain period. Everglow 1.5 shows these characters as they are.
Media references.
Where a photo, video or recording sat, the text keeps a line such as ![](dayone-moment://…), but the file itself isn’t imported.
Time zones.

Everglow keeps the exact moment of each entry and shows it in your iPhone’s current time zone. Day One also records the time zone you wrote in, which Everglow doesn’t use, so an entry written near midnight while traveling can appear on the neighboring day.
What stays in Day One
Photos, videos, audio recordings and PDF attachments.
Location and weather.
Favorite and pinned marks.
Journal names. Entries from every journal you import share one Everglow timeline.
Everglow’s import reads a copy of the export file and changes nothing in Day One. Keep your Day One journal and the export file until you have checked the result.
Will my photos come over?

No. Everglow 1.5 imports the text of each entry and leaves photos, videos, audio and PDFs behind, with a placeholder line where each one was. Keep Day One, or a JSON or PDF export from it, for your media.
Will my dates be kept?

Yes. Day One’s JSON export stores each entry’s date and time in a standard format that Everglow reads exactly, so entries land on the days you wrote them. Everglow shows those moments in your iPhone’s current time zone, so check any entry written near midnight in another time zone.
Can I keep using Day One?

Yes. Everglow doesn’t connect to Day One or change it, so new Day One entries need a fresh export. When you import again, entries whose text and day are unchanged are skipped, and an entry you edited in Day One comes in as another entry beside the earlier one.
What if my journal is very large?

Import it in batches by date range. The engine you choose reads every entry: on-device keeps your text on your iPhone but is slower, Everglow Cloud uses its monthly allowance and pauses if that runs out, and your own API key sends entry text to that provider. Beyond 7 entries you need Everglow Unlimited, a one-time purchase ($9.99 in the US), or an active Everglow Cloud subscription. A paused import waits in the notification bell and resumes where it stopped.
Can I move my entries out of Everglow later?
Yes. Settings → Export your journal creates a ZIP of plain Markdown files, one per dated entry, with your conversations alongside. The file is unencrypted, so store it somewhere private.

own-api-key-journal: Can I use my own API key in an AI journal?
Yes. Everglow for iPhone works with your own OpenAI, Claude, Gemini or DeepSeek API key, and a one-time purchase removes its limits. No Everglow subscription is needed.
With your own key, Everglow charges for the app and your AI provider charges for the AI work. Everglow is not part of the provider’s billing.

free to download, with 7 journal entries and 10 companion chat turns to try it. Everglow Unlimited is a one-time purchase, $9.99 in the US, that removes both limits permanently. Prices vary by storefront, and the app shows the current one.
requests go to your provider under your key, and the provider bills that usage to your account at its own rates. Everglow adds no fee per request.
Everglow Cloud, the optional hosted-AI subscription, or an Everglow account. Everglow doesn’t ask you to create one.
Unlimited means unlimited entries and companion chat turns. It does not include hosted AI, and it does not pay for your provider’s usage.
Everglow 1.5 supports four providers. Each one uses a single fixed model, shown under its name in the app. There is no model picker, and other providers or self-hosted models can’t be added.
To estimate what you’ll pay, look these models up on your provider’s pricing page.
You can choose your own key during first-run setup:
On the setup step that offers three ways to run the AI, tap
, the option for bringing your own key.
Pick Claude, DeepSeek, Gemini or OpenAI.
The first time you choose a cloud engine, a one-time sheet titled
explains that the entries the model reads are sent to that provider, and links each provider’s privacy policy. Confirm to continue, or tap Not now.
. Everglow checks the key with the provider before saving it and tells you if the key isn’t valid or the provider can’t be reached. That check carries no journal text.
On an iPhone without enough memory for the on-device model, setup goes straight to the list of cloud options.

To add a key later or change providers, open Settings, and under Privacy & Data tap the row that names your current engine. In the AI ENGINE list, choose a provider, paste its key in the field that opens and tap Save. You can switch engines at any time. Keys for several providers can be saved side by side, so switching back to one doesn’t ask for its key again.
What gets sent, and what doesn’t

Your journal archive stays on your iPhone, and the search that finds relevant entries runs there too. Each AI request carries the context one task needs and goes from your iPhone straight to the provider’s API. It does not pass through an Everglow server.

Everglow reads it in the background with several requests, for its summary, the people and places in it, facts, relationships, dates and topics. Each carries that entry’s text, and some also carry the names Everglow already knows so it can match them.

your question and the entries the search found go to the provider in small batches so the model can judge which are relevant, and up to 12 of them are used to write the answer. Long entries are cut to an excerpt around the match.
your message, the recent conversation, the companion’s instructions and a short context block with brief summaries of related entries and notes on people you mention.
a person’s page is written from what several entries say about them, and a monthly summary from that month’s entry summaries.

when Everglow offers to re-read older entries after an update, the offer says it will send them through your provider, one call each, using your own API credit. An import’s review screen names the engine that will process it.

The whole archive is never sent in a single request, and your key goes only to the provider it belongs to. Everglow never uses your writing to train any model. What the provider does with the requests it receives is set by its own terms.

The key is saved in the iOS Keychain and set to stay on this iPhone. It isn’t synced through iCloud Keychain, isn’t part of Everglow’s optional iCloud backup, and doesn’t move to a new iPhone, where you paste it again. Everglow 1.5 has no separate button to delete a key: paste a new one to replace it, switch engines to stop using it, or revoke it in your provider’s dashboard to disable it everywhere.

Claude (Anthropic), DeepSeek, Gemini (Google) and OpenAI. In Everglow 1.5 they use claude-haiku-4-5, deepseek-flash, gemini-2.5-flash and gpt-5.4-mini. Other providers and self-hosted models aren’t supported.

It is stored in this iPhone’s Keychain, set never to leave the device, and is sent only to its own provider over HTTPS. Anyone who can open Everglow on your iPhone can use the AI it pays for, so consider turning on the app lock.
Does Everglow see my key or my journal?

No. With your own key, requests go from your iPhone straight to the provider and don’t pass through an Everglow server. The app’s App Store privacy label is “Data Not Collected.” Your provider does receive the context each request carries.
Do I still need to buy something?
Not to try it: the free 7 entries and 10 companion chat turns work with your own key. To go past them, buy Everglow Unlimited once, $9.99 in the US. Everglow Cloud is optional and not needed.
How much will my provider charge?

It depends on your provider’s prices and on how much you write, ask and chat. Each saved entry is read with several requests, and each question and chat reply uses more. Your provider’s usage page shows what you actually spend.

on-device-ai-journal-iphone: On-device AI
How does on-device AI journaling work on iPhone?
Everglow downloads Google’s Gemma 4 E2B model once, about 2.6 GB, and runs it on your iPhone with Google’s LiteRT-LM runtime. Your writing isn’t sent anywhere for AI.
Verified against Everglow 1.5 on 10 October 2026.
At a glance
Part
Everglow 1.5
Model
Gemma 4 E2B, the instruction-tuned build in .litertlm format
Source
litert-community
on Hugging Face
Runtime
LiteRT-LM
from Google, built into the app
Download
About 2.6 GB, once, over Wi-Fi only
Integrity check
SHA-256 hash of one pinned file revision
Compute
GPU through Metal by default, CPU as an option
Context budget
32,768 or 24,576 tokens, set by the phone’s memory
Model requests
One at a time
Search index
Built on the phone, without Gemma
Setting it up

During setup, Everglow offers three ways to run its AI: on this phone, Everglow Cloud, or your own API key. Choosing the phone starts the model download from Hugging Face. Here is what the download does.
It uses Wi-Fi only, never cellular data.
It keeps the screen from locking while it runs, and you can keep using the app. If you leave Everglow, it may remind you that the download finishes faster with the app open.
If the connection drops partway, the app keeps what it already has and offers to resume. If the partial file can’t be used, it offers to start over.
Before the model is loaded, the app checks the file against the SHA-256 hash of the exact revision it expects. A file that doesn’t match is deleted, not loaded.

If Hugging Face doesn’t answer, the app tries a mirror, hf-mirror.com, held to the same check. If no download server answers, which the app notes is common in mainland China, it says so and offers DeepSeek, a cloud model, instead.

The model is kept in the app’s own storage, apart from your journal, so Everglow’s iCloud backup doesn’t include it. On a new iPhone you download it again. You can delete it in Settings to free the space.
How your iPhone’s memory matters
Setup checks how much memory the phone has. If there isn’t enough for the model, setup doesn’t offer on-device AI, says why, and offers Everglow Cloud or your own API key instead.

Memory also sets the context budget: how many tokens the model can hold at once, counting both what it reads and what it writes. Phones that report at least 6.5 GB of memory get 32,768 tokens; others get 24,576. Because the budget is shared, a very long entry or a long conversation leaves less room for the reply.
What runs on the model
Reading each new entry.
In the background, the model writes a short summary and picks out the feeling, the people, places and things mentioned, and the topics.
Ask.

Search finds candidate passages and the model keeps the relevant ones. It then writes the answer from a capped amount of evidence, about 6,000 tokens and usually no more than 12 entries, and shows the dated excerpts it used.
The companion.

Replies in chat draw on relevant entries. On the phone, the conversation stays loaded between turns instead of being re-read each time. In a very long chat, the oldest turns drop out of the model’s working memory and the recent ones stay.
People pages.
Facts about the people, places and things you write about, each linked to the entry it came from.
Find the date.
Working out when something you describe happened.
What doesn’t use the model
Writing, editing, bookmarks and keyword search.
The vectors behind search by meaning. Everglow computes them on the phone with Apple’s NaturalLanguage framework, not with Gemma.
Drawing the relationship map. The people and ties on it come from earlier reading; arranging them is plain code.
Markdown export, iCloud backup and app lock.
One request at a time

The phone runs one model request at a time. When you chat or ask a question, that request goes first; background reading waits, or stops and runs again afterward. A large import is read entry by entry. The app’s own note says a few hundred entries can take a while, and an import picks up where it left off if you quit the app. For a single import, you can choose another engine you’ve already set up.
Apple Intelligence isn’t involved

Everglow ships its own model and runtime. In version 1.5, none of its AI features use Apple Intelligence or Apple’s Foundation Models framework, so on-device AI in Everglow doesn’t depend on Apple Intelligence being available or turned on. It depends on the model download, the phone’s memory and free storage.
The trade-offs
Speed and battery.
On-device AI is slower than hosted AI and uses more battery. The app’s setup screen lists both as the cost of this option.
Storage.
About 2.6 GB for the model, on top of the app.
Depth.
It is a small model with a bounded context. Hosted AI is usually faster and handles longer, more detailed questions better.
Accuracy.
Any AI can get details wrong. Ask shows the dated excerpts it used, so you can check them against your entries.
GPU or CPU.
The model runs on the GPU through Metal unless you turn that off in Settings, where the app notes the GPU is faster on most devices. The change applies after you restart the app.
Privacy with on-device AI

With on-device AI, your entries are processed on the iPhone and nothing is sent anywhere for AI. The journal archive is stored on the phone whichever engine you use. Downloading the model sends no journal content. iCloud backup is a separate, optional choice. The first time you switch to Everglow Cloud or your own API key, the app asks for your consent and names the provider.
Does on-device AI work without internet?

Yes, after the one-time model download. Writing, Ask and the companion work offline with the on-device model. You need a connection for the download, for Everglow Cloud or your own API key, and for iCloud backup.
Will it run on my iPhone?
Everglow needs iOS 17 or later. For on-device AI, setup checks the phone’s memory. If there isn’t enough, setup says so and offers Everglow Cloud or your own API key. Speed varies by device.
How much space does it take?
About 2.6 GB for the model, plus the app itself, which the App Store lists at about 90 MB. You can delete the model in Settings; using on-device AI again means downloading it again.
Can I switch to hosted AI later?
Yes. In Settings you can switch between on-device AI, Everglow Cloud and your own API key at any time, and the downloaded model stays available unless you delete it.
Is the model the same as ChatGPT?

No. On-device mode runs Google’s Gemma 4 E2B on your iPhone, not an OpenAI model. Everglow Cloud sends requests through Everglow’s service to OpenAI, and you can also use your own OpenAI key. Both are remote processing.
Does Everglow use Apple Intelligence?
No. Everglow 1.5 ships its own model and runtime, and its AI features don’t use Apple Intelligence or Apple’s Foundation Models framework.

privacy: Privacy Policy
Last updated: July 18, 2026
Everglow is built to be a private place to think. Your journal lives on your device, and nothing leaves it unless you explicitly turn on a feature that requires it.
The short version
By default we don't run servers, and we don't collect, see, or store your data. The one exception is Everglow Cloud, an optional hosted-AI subscription you can turn on (details below).
There is no analytics, no tracking, no advertising, and no third-party SDKs harvesting your activity.
Your journal entries, chats, and the people and places Everglow recognizes are stored locally on your device.
The built-in AI companion runs entirely on-device — your writing is processed locally.
Three optional features can send data off-device, and all are off by default: Everglow Cloud, third-party AI providers, and iCloud backup.
What we collect

Nothing, by default. For the core app, Everglow has no backend operated by us; we do not have accounts, and we never receive your journal content, usage data, device identifiers, or personal information. The one exception is the optional Everglow Cloud subscription (below): when you use it, the content of a request passes through Everglow's hosted service to generate your reply and is not retained after the request completes.
What stays on your device
All of your content is stored locally in the app's private storage, including:
Journal entries, photos, and any audio you add.
Chat conversations with the companion.
The entities (people, places, things) and connections Everglow derives from your writing.
Your settings and preferences.
Any API keys you enter are stored securely in the device Keychain. If you set an app-lock password, only a one-way hash of it is stored — never the password itself.
On-device AI
By default, Everglow's AI features are powered by a language model that runs entirely on your device. Your entries and chats are processed locally and are not transmitted anywhere for this to work.
Optional: third-party AI providers

If you prefer, you can connect Everglow to a third-party AI provider — such as Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI, Google (Gemini), or DeepSeek — by entering your own API key. This is entirely optional and off by default.

When you enable a remote provider, the journal or chat content needed to fulfill your request is sent directly from your device to that provider for processing. That data is then handled under that provider's privacy policy and terms, not ours. We are not an intermediary and do not see this traffic. You can switch back to the on-device model at any time.
Optional: Everglow Cloud (hosted AI)

You can optionally subscribe to Everglow Cloud, a hosted AI option operated by Everglow. Unlike the on-device model and unlike bringing your own key, this routes through Everglow's own servers. When it is your chosen engine, the journal or chat content needed for your request is sent — encrypted in transit — to Everglow's servers, which process it using OpenAI as our sub-processor to generate your reply. Everglow retains no content after the request completes and never uses your writing to train any model. Once your content reaches OpenAI, it is also handled under OpenAI's own privacy policy. Everglow Cloud is optional, off by default, and you can switch back to the on-device model at any time.
Optional: iCloud backup

You may turn on iCloud backup to protect your journal and move it between your own devices. When enabled, Everglow bundles your data into a single encrypted snapshot stored in your private iCloud (CloudKit) account. This data lives in your own Apple iCloud storage under Apple's privacy terms; we have no access to it. Disabling backup and deleting the snapshot removes it from iCloud.
Children's privacy
Everglow is not directed to children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect information from them. Because no data is collected by us, the app does not gather personal information from any user.
Changes to this policy
If we change how the app handles data, we'll update this page and revise the date above. Material changes will be reflected in the app where appropriate.

Everglow 旨在成为一个属于你的私密思考空间。你的日记存储在你的设备上，除非你主动开启某项需要联网的功能，否则任何内容都不会离开设备。
简要说明
默认情况下，我们不运营任何服务器，也不会收集、查看或存储你的数据。唯一的例外是 Everglow 云端——一项你可选择开启的托管 AI 订阅（详见下文）。
没有任何分析统计、行为追踪、广告，也没有第三方 SDK 采集你的使用行为。
你的日记、对话，以及 Everglow 识别出的人物和地点，都保存在你的设备本地。
内置的 AI 伙伴完全在设备本地运行——你写下的内容也在本地处理。
有三项可选功能会将数据发送到设备之外，且默认均为关闭：Everglow 云端、第三方 AI 服务和 iCloud 备份。
我们收集哪些信息
默认不收集任何信息。就核心应用而言，Everglow 没有由我们运营的后端服务；我们没有账户体系，也绝不会获取你的日记内容、使用数据、设备标识或个人信息。唯一的例外是可选的 Everglow 云端订阅（见下文）：当你使用它时，请求所含的内容会经由 Everglow 的托管服务处理以生成回复，并在请求完成后不予保留。
哪些内容保存在你的设备上
你的全部内容都保存在应用的私有本地存储中，包括：
日记、照片，以及你添加的任何音频。
与 AI 伙伴的对话。
Everglow 从你的文字中提炼出的实体（人物、地点、事物）及其关联。
你的设置与偏好。
你输入的任何 API 密钥都会安全地保存在设备的钥匙串（Keychain）中。如果你设置了应用锁密码，仅会保存其单向哈希值，绝不会保存密码本身。
设备端 AI
默认情况下，Everglow 的 AI 功能由一个完全在你设备上运行的语言模型驱动。你的日记和对话均在本地处理，无需将其传输到任何地方即可工作。
可选项：第三方 AI 服务
如果你愿意，可以通过输入自己的 API 密钥，将 Everglow 连接到第三方 AI 服务——例如 Anthropic（Claude）、OpenAI、Google（Gemini）或 DeepSeek。此功能完全可选，且默认关闭。
当你启用某个远程服务时，为完成你的请求所需的日记或对话内容，会直接从你的设备发送给该服务商进行处理。这些数据随后将依据该服务商的隐私政策和条款处理，而非我们的。我们不是中间方，也无法看到这些流量。你可以随时切换回设备端模型。
可选项：Everglow 云端（托管 AI）

你可以选择订阅 Everglow 云端——一项由 Everglow 运营的托管 AI 服务。与设备端模型不同，也与自带密钥不同，它会经由 Everglow 自己的服务器处理。当它作为你选用的引擎时，为完成你的请求所需的日记或对话内容，会经加密传输发送至 Everglow 的服务器，并由其使用 OpenAI 作为我们的子处理方进行处理以生成回复。Everglow 在请求完成后不保留任何内容，也绝不会用你的文字训练任何模型。当你的内容抵达 OpenAI 后，还将依据 OpenAI 自身的隐私政策处理。Everglow 云端完全可选，默认关闭，你可以随时切换回设备端模型。
可选项：iCloud 备份
你可以开启 iCloud 备份，以保护日记并在自己的设备之间迁移。开启后，Everglow 会将你的数据打包成一份加密快照，存入你的私人 iCloud（CloudKit）账户。这些数据存放在你自己的 Apple iCloud 存储中，受 Apple 隐私条款约束；我们无权访问。关闭备份并删除该快照即可将其从 iCloud 中移除。
儿童隐私
Everglow 并非面向 13 岁以下儿童，我们也不会有意收集他们的信息。由于我们不收集任何数据，本应用不会从任何用户处采集个人信息。
本政策的变更
如果我们更改了应用处理数据的方式，会更新本页面并修订上方的日期。重大变更将在应用内适当位置予以体现。
